notes: T477 (does the dispatcher heal the task whose worker it just watched die?) — answered yes. When bin/subagent's verification fails AND the worker died (rc != 0) leaving the kanban row in_progress, the dispatcher now reopens it (managent reopen), writes a JSON assertion record (task_id, model, exit_code, wall_seconds, healed_by=dispatcher, timestamp) to docs/infra/dispatch-heals.jsonl (WEIZIGO_DISPATCH_HEALS override for tests), and prints one [verify] line so the operator sees the heal. Heal lives in tools/dispatch_verify.py:heal_dispatch, invoked from bin/subagent after a failed verification; bin/ollama-subagent and bin/subagent-ds wrap bin/subagent, so both front doors heal. Guards: heals ONLY when status==in_progress AND rc!=0 (the watched-die case). Never heals: a lazy worker (row still dispatchable), a successful worker (row done), or a deliverable failure (row done — left untouched as a claim to investigate). The tree is never touched. Test-first: tools/regression-dispatch-verification.sh gained a die stub mode (claims then exits 124) and a sabotage mode (done --status pass then deletes the deliverable); new arms 5 (seeded: die->healed, assertion written), 2b (die heals via ollama-subagent too), 6 (second null: deliverable failure -> task untouched, no heal), plus no-heal assertions on the lazy (arm 1) and honest (arm 4) controls. Shown red before the fix (arm 5 failed on heal-line/status/assertion; nulls already passed), green after. regression-dispatch-verification: ALL CONTROLS PASSED, in-suite (zig build test); 0 FAIL lines in the dispatch-verification block. The zig build test exit 1 is an unrelated engine calibration failure (I4 2x2 CALIBRATION, src/ — not touched by this task).
